DOCTOR VISIT LESSON · DOCTOR VISIT · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Reception Desk — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the reception desk as the visit’s front door: one friendly hello, one name, and the waiting begins.

What is this?

The reception desk is the desk at the front of the clinic where a helper greets families and lets the doctor know you have arrived.

What does it mean?

The desk is where a stranger becomes a helper with a face. Children who have rehearsed "hello, we are here" walk in as participants, not packages.

What does the child need to know?

You need the card and a possible script: "hello, we are here — this is [name]." That is the whole line. The child says any part of it they like, even just the name.

Why this matters

First impressions run both ways: a child who has greeted the room settles faster, and a settled child makes every later step — the scale, the stethoscope — easier.

What it teaches

Social scripts (greeting, answering "who is here?"), speaking to new adults from a safe distance, and the pride of having a job at the desk.

Words to learn

reception deskreceptionisthelloarrivecheck inname

Say this to your child

“"Reception desk! We tell the receptionist our name. Hello — we are here! She will tell the doctor, and the doctor will be so happy to see you."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "the reception desk is where we say we have arrived."
  2. Rehearse the line at home: "hello, we are here!" — with a wave.
  3. At the real desk, let your child say their own name if they want to; whisper it to you is also fine.
  4. Point out the helper’s name tag and read it together.
  5. Then: "now we wait for our turn" — and on to the waiting-room lesson.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "reception desk — we tell the receptionist our name" sit over a child and parent at a curved front desk, the receptionist waving from behind a computer.

Ask your child

"Who sits at the reception desk?" "What do we say when we arrive?" "Whose name does the helper wear on a tag?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might practice the hello in the car the whole way there, hand over a toy "appointment card," or whisper the name like a secret password.

Out in the real world

Every office has a front desk — the library, the pool, the dentist. The same hello works at all of them, and it gets easier every time.

Try it together

Front Desk: a table, a toy phone, a notebook. Every stuffed animal arrives and checks in by name; your child is the receptionist — then swap, and now the child arrives and the grown-up greets. Both sides of the desk, both jobs practiced.

Understanding check

Ask: "What do we do at the desk?" (say hello — we are here) "Who is behind the desk?" (a helper) "What happens after the hello?" (we wait for our turn)

Staying safe

Never promise "the receptionist will be nice" as a deal — describe what happens: we say hello, she says hello. Routines, not bargains, are what hold steady in new rooms.

This lesson pairs with the Reception Desk flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Doctor Visit.
